frs_sections.title: Scope and Introduction
frs_sections.content:
========================
PROFIBUS (Process Field Bus) is an open industrial fieldbus standard for
distributed automation. It is standardized internationally in IEC 61158
(the Type 3 fieldbus, defining the physical layer, data-link layer and
application layer services) and IEC 61784-1 (Communication Profile Family
3, CPF 3, which selects the protocol subsets for the real communication
profiles). PROFIBUS was originally specified as the German national
standard DIN 19245 and the European standard EN 50170, and is maintained
by PROFIBUS & PROFINET International (PI), formerly the PROFIBUS Nutzer
Organisation (PNO).

PROFIBUS comes in two principal communication profiles plus a legacy
profile:

  * PROFIBUS-DP (Decentralized Periphery) — the dominant profile. A fast,
    cyclic master-slave pr…

frs_sections.title: Architecture and Layering
frs_sections.content:
===========================
PROFIBUS follows a reduced OSI layering model. Only three layers are
implemented for DP:

  Layer 1 — Physical Layer (PHY): RS-485 (IEC 61158-2 Type 3 / EIA-485)
            for DP, or MBP (Manchester Bus Powered, IEC 61158-2) for PA.
  Layer 2 — Data-Link Layer: the Fieldbus Data Link (FDL), which provides
            the hybrid token-passing + master-slave Medium Access Control
            (MAC) and the telegram framing, addressing and checksum.
  Layer 7 — Application Layer: the DP services (DPV0 cyclic data exchange,
            DPV1 acyclic read/write and alarms, DPV2 isochronous and
            slave-to-slave) and the Direct Data Link Mapper (DDLM) /
            User Interface that the field-device application sees.

Layers 3-6 are empty (not used). The ap…

frs_sections.title: Physical Layer
frs_sections.content:
================
3.1 RS-485 Transmission (PROFIBUS-DP, the H2 / electrical PHY)
-------------------------------------------------------------
The DP physical layer is a balanced (differential) two-wire RS-485 line,
designated the A-line and B-line, in a linear bus (daisy-chain) topology
with active bus termination at both ends. Key parameters:

  * Medium: shielded twisted-pair copper cable (PROFIBUS cable type A).
  * Signaling: differential NRZ, half-duplex, balanced per EIA/RS-485.
  * Connector: 9-pin D-sub (DB9) or M12; pin 3 = B-line (RxD/TxD-P),
    pin 8 = A-line (RxD/TxD-N).
  * Bus termination: 220 ohm pull termination network with 390 ohm
    pull-up to +5 V (VP, pin 6) and 390 ohm pull-down to DGND (pin 5),
    enabled at the two physical ends of the segment.

frs_sections.title: Timers
frs_sections.content:
----------
  * TSL — Slot Time: the maximum time the sender waits for the start of
    the addressed station's response before assuming no answer.
  * TID1/TID2 — Idle Times after a transaction.
  * TTR — Target Rotation Time (token-ring budget).
  * TSDR — Station Delay of Responder (min/max time a responder waits
    before it may send its reply).

5 Telegram (Frame) Formats
==========================
PROFIBUS data-link telegrams are byte-oriented. Each telegram begins with
a Start Delimiter (SD) byte that selects the telegram format, and (for
the variable/fixed data telegrams) ends with a Frame Check Sequence (FCS)
and an End Delimiter (ED = 0x16).

frs_sections.title: Telegram fields
frs_sections.content:
-------------------
  * DA  — Destination Address (1 octet; station address 0-127, bit 7 is
    the EXT bit indicating that a DSAP/SSAP service-access-point byte
    follows in the data unit).
  * SA  — Source Address (1 octet; with EXT bit for SSAP presence).
  * FC  — Frame Control (1 octet): encodes the frame type (Send/Request
    SRD or SDN, Request-FDL-Status, Token), the Frame Count Bit (FCB) and
    Frame-Count-Bit-Valid (FCV) for duplicate/lost-frame detection, and
    the station type (master/slave) and FDL state.
  * DSAP — Destination Service Access Point (selects the DP service at the
    receiver; present when DA.EXT = 1).
  * SSAP — Source Service Access Point (selects the service at the sender;
    present when SA.EXT = 1). Default SAP (no DSAP/SSAP byte) is used for
    th…

frs_sections.title: Diagnostics
frs_sections.content:
=============
DP provides a standardized, layered diagnostic mechanism. A slave returns
diagnostic information in response to the Slave_Diag (Get_Diag) service:
  * Station-related diagnostics (6 mandatory bytes): station status 1/2/3,
    master address (the address of the master that parameterized the
    slave) and the Ident_Number.
  * Module-related (identifier) diagnostics — a bit per configured module
    indicating which module raised a diagnosis.
  * Channel-related diagnostics — per-channel error type (e.g. short
    circuit, under/over-voltage, overtemperature, line break).
  * Device/extended (manufacturer) diagnostics — vendor-specific.
A slave signals "new diagnostics available" via the response so the master
re-reads the full diagnostic frame.

frs_sections.title: Addressing
frs_sections.content:
=============
  * Station addresses are 0 to 126 (7 bits in DA/SA; address 127 = 0x7F
    is reserved as the broadcast/global address). Address 126 is the
    factory default delivery address used with Set_Slave_Address.
  * Up to 126 stations addressable on a network (with repeaters).
  * Up to 32 stations per RS-485 segment without a repeater.

protocol_overview.type: Industrial fieldbus (IEC 61158 Type 3 / IEC 61784-1 CPF 3). PROFIBUS-DP is a cyclic master-slave protocol with a hybrid token-passing + master-slave medium-access control over RS-485 (DP) or MBP (PA).
protocol_overview.duplex: Half-duplex on the shared RS-485 bus (one differential pair); only the token holder transmits and a polled slave responds within the slot time. PROFIBUS-PA is half-duplex on the bus-powered MBP pair.
protocol_overview.medium_access: Hybrid: active stations (masters) pass a token in a logical ring (ascending address order, bounded by the Target Rotation Time TTR); the token holder polls its passive stations (slaves), which only respond when addressed.

physical_layers.phy: MBP / IEC 61158-2, Manchester, bus-powered, intrinsically safe

protocol_overview.character_format: 11-bit UART character: 1 start bit + 8 data bits + 1 even parity bit + 1 stop bit.

compliance_requirements: RS-485 (DP) and/or MBP (PA) physical layer per IEC 61158-2.
Telegram family SD1/SD2/SD3/SD4 + SC short ACK + ED=0x16; DA/SA/FC/DSAP/SSAP/DU/FCS fields; 8-bit checksum FCS.
DP service levels DPV0 (cyclic) and, where claimed, DPV1 (acyclic + alarms) and DPV2 (isochronous + slave-to-slave).
GSD device description with a PI-assigned Ident_Number.
Station addressing 0..126 (127 broadcast); <=32 per segment, <=126 per network.

DPV1 — Acyclic Data Exchange and Alarms

functional_requirements.text: PROFIBUS-DP provides a balanced differential RS-485 two-wire line (A-line / B-line) in a linear bus, half-duplex NRZ, at selectable baud rates 9.6/19.2/45.45/93.75/187.5/500 kbit/s and 1.5/3/6/12 Mbit/s, with active 220 ohm bus termination at both segment ends.

PROFIBUS-PA provides an MBP / IEC 61158-2 Manchester-encoded, bus-powered, intrinsically-safe physical layer at a fixed 31.25 kbit/s for hazardous (Ex) areas, coupled to the DP backbone via a DP/PA coupler or link.

The data-link layer (FDL) uses a hybrid medium-access method: active masters pass a token in a logical ring ordered by station address (bounded by the Target Rotation Time TTR), and the token holder polls its passive slaves in a master-slave manner; this supports multi-master operation.

Telegrams are byte-oriented and selected by a Start Delimiter: SD1=0x10 (fixed length, no data), SD2=0x68 (variable length with data), SD3=0xA2 (fixed length with 8 data octets), SD4=0xDC (token). A single-byte short acknowledgement is SC=0xE5; data/fixed telegrams end with an 8-bit FCS and the End Delimiter ED=0x16.

A telegram carries a Destination Address (DA), Source Address (SA), Frame Control (FC, including the Frame Count Bit FCB and FCB-Valid FCV for duplicate detection), optional Destination/Source Service Access Points (DSAP/SSAP, present when the address EXT bit is set), a Data Unit (DU, 0..246 octets), and the 8-bit Frame Check Sequence (FCS).

DPV0 provides deterministic cyclic data exchange: the DP Class-1 master parameterizes (Set_Prm) and checks configuration (Chk_Cfg) of each slave, then cyclically writes outputs to and reads inputs from the slaves (Data_Exchange), plus standard diagnostics and Global_Control SYNC/FREEZE.

DPV1 adds acyclic read/write of slave data records addressed by Slot and Index (MSAC_C1 from a Class-1 master and MSAC_C2 via an explicit Class-2 connection: Initiate/Data_Transport/Abort) and acknowledged alarm handling (process / diagnostic / pull-plug / status / update alarms).
DPV2 adds isochronous (clock-synchronous, equidistant) operation and slave-to-slave Data Exchange Broadcast (DXB, publisher/subscriber), plus time stamping and redundancy services.

Each station is described by a GSD (General Station Description) file declaring vendor / model / Ident_Number, supported baud rates and bus timing, the module / configuration (Cfg) identifier bytes, and the user parameter bytes, so an engineering tool configures the device driverlessly.

A slave returns layered diagnostics in response to Slave_Diag (Get_Diag): station-related (6 mandatory bytes incl. master address and Ident_Number), module/identifier-related, channel-related (per-channel error type), and device/extended (manufacturer-specific).

A DP slave follows the startup state machine POWER_ON -> Wait_Prm -> Wait_Cfg -> Data_Exchange driven by the master; a watchdog supervises the master's cyclic access and a Global_Control CLEAR or watchdog timeout forces a safe/cleared output state.

Station addresses span 0..126 (7-bit DA/SA; 127 = broadcast). Up to 32 stations attach per RS-485 segment without a repeater and up to 126 addressable stations per network with repeaters; address 126 is the delivery default used with Set_Slave_Address.

error_response_conditions: FCS (8-bit checksum) mismatch — the telegram is rejected (no/wrong response).
Slot-time (TSL) expiry — the responder did not answer in time; the master retries.
Frame Count Bit (FCB/FCV) mismatch — duplicate or lost telegram detection.
Parameterization (Set_Prm) or configuration (Chk_Cfg) mismatch — the slave does not enter Data_Exchange (stays in Wait_Prm / Wait_Cfg).
Watchdog timeout — the slave loses cyclic access from its master and goes to a safe/cleared output state.
New diagnostics available — the slave flags it and the master re-reads the full diagnostic telegram (Slave_Diag).
